<role>
You write a one-page opportunity brief for a Keelwater product manager. Keelwater makes claims-handling software. You use only the facts and customer insights below.
</role>
<opportunity>
{
 "title": "Missing multi-payee payment split option",
 "problem_statement": "Users cannot find a way to divide a single claim payment among multiple recipients. This prevents them from processing claims that require distributing funds to several parties."
}
</opportunity>
<fact_sheet>
{
 "as_of": "2026-11-03",
 "accounts_n": 1,
 "mentions_n": 2,
 "routes_n": 1,
 "mentions_by_route": {
  "account_management": 2
 },
 "arr_total_gbp": 60000.0,
 "renewals_90d_n": 0,
 "accounts": [
  {
   "name": "Farrowdene Home",
   "arr_gbp": 60000.0,
   "renewal_date": "2027-06-02",
   "mentions": 2
  }
 ]
}
</fact_sheet>
<insights>
[
 {
  "id": "4dc69dfc59fb39bc",
  "quote": "We’ve got a claim where we need to split a payment across several payees — not sure how to handle that in the system.",
  "account": "Farrowdene Home",
  "route": "account_management",
  "date": "2026-10-19T11:22:00+00:00"
 },
 {
  "id": "6b5fec6f43e17fc0",
  "quote": "I’m not seeing the option under payments or tasks right now.",
  "account": "Farrowdene Home",
  "route": "account_management",
  "date": "2026-10-19T11:22:00+00:00"
 }
]
</insights>
<rules>
- Cite every insight you rely on as [i:INSIGHT_ID], using the id exactly as given. Cite at least three different insights when three or more are given, and cover every route that appears.
- Use these sections, in this order, as Markdown headings: "## Problem", "## Who is affected", "## Evidence", "## Why now".
- Every bullet under "Who is affected" and "Evidence" ends with a citation. Every sentence that contains a number or a date carries a citation.
- Copy every account count, mention count, route count, renewal count and ARR figure from the fact sheet. Never compute, add up or round a number yourself; write an ARR figure only as it appears in the fact sheet, in pounds.
- Write counts as digits exactly as the fact sheet gives them ("5 accounts", never "five accounts"); never write "one customer" or "a single customer" unless the fact sheet count says 1 for that same thing.
- Put text in quotation marks only when it is a customer quote copied word for word, character for character, from one insight cited in the same sentence. Never put quotation marks around a paraphrase, a fragment of your own wording or a phrase from the fact sheet; when unsure, paraphrase without quotation marks.
- Name a customer only when a cited insight in the same sentence belongs to that customer.
- Do not claim more than the evidence shows: no "all customers", no scope wider than the cited accounts, and mention any cited insight that points the other way.
- Do not recommend a solution.
</rules>
<output>
JSON only: {"body_md": the brief as Markdown, "citations": the list of insight ids you cited}
</output>

{"body_md": "## Problem

Users cannot find a way to divide a single claim payment among multiple recipients, which prevents them from processing claims that require distributing funds to several parties.

## Who is affected

- Farrowdene Home, an account with 60000.0 GBP in ARR and a renewal date of 2027-06-02, raised this need twice [i:4dc69dfc59fb39bc] [i:6b5fec6f43e17fc0].
- The affected scope in the fact sheet is 1 account, with 2 mentions across 1 route, account_management [i:4dc69dfc59fb39bc] [i:6b5fec6f43e17fc0].

## Evidence

- Farrowdene Home said they have a claim where they need to split a payment across several payees and are not sure how to handle that in the system [i:4dc69dfc59fb39bc].
- Farrowdene Home also said they are not seeing the option under payments or tasks right now [i:6b5fec6f43e17fc0].
- Both mentions came through the account_management route, and the fact sheet records 0 renewals in the next 90 days [i:4dc69dfc59fb39bc] [i:6b5fec6f43e17fc0].

## Why now

- The fact sheet is dated 2026-11-03 and records 1 account, 2 mentions and 1 route, with 60000.0 GBP in ARR tied to Farrowdene Home [i:4dc69dfc59fb39bc] [i:6b5fec6f43e17fc0].
- Farrowdene Home's renewal date is 2027-06-02, and the fact sheet shows 0 renewals in the next 90 days [i:4dc69dfc59fb39bc] [i:6b5fec6f43e17fc0].
- No cited insight points the other way; the evidence is limited to this account and route [i:4dc69dfc59fb39bc] [i:6b5fec6f43e17fc0].
", "citations": ["4dc69dfc59fb39bc", "6b5fec6f43e17fc0"]}
